title: Pathophysiology
description: The course focuses on disease processes in the human body from a systems approach. Analysis of the most common and significant diseases is included. The signs and symptoms, etiology, diagnosis, and treatment of disease are examined along with the appropriate medical terminology. This course is designed for students in allied health programs, but is also open to those who wish to broaden their medical background or review this information.
outcomes: Identify common and significant medical conditions and diseases and their signs, symptoms, and etiology.
Identify common medical conditions and diseases and their signs, symptoms and etiology.
objectives: Describe common and significant medical conditions and diseases.
Distinguish the elementary pathophysiology and characteristics of diseases presented including signs, symptoms, etiology, diagnosis and treatment.
Identify and select the basic laboratory and radiological tests used in the diagnosis of disease conditions.
Differentiate medications commonly used in the diseases and conditions presented.
content: Diseases and conditions of the endocrine system
Diseases and conditions of the eye and ear
Disease and conditions of the integumentary system
Diseases and conditions of the musculoskeletal system
Diseases and conditions of the digestive system
Diseases and conditions of the oral cavity
Diseases of the liver, biliary tract and pancreas
Disorders of nutrient intake and absorption
Diseases and conditions of the respiratory system
Diseases and conditions of the circulatory system
Diseases and conditions of the urinary system
Diseases and conditions of the reproductive systems
Disorders and conditions resulting from trauma
Cumulative trauma (repetitive motion trauma, overuse syndromes)
assignments: Related textbooks (including the Language of Medicine and Comprehensive Medical Terminology).
Professional journals (including the American Journal of Nursing).
Related reference books (Merck Manual of Diagnosis and Treatment and Physician's Desk Reference).
Internet sites related to common medical conditions and diseases.
Abstracting medical information from text and other medical material.
Translating medical material into non-medical language.
Analyzing signs, symptoms, etiology, diagnostic tests and treatment of disease conditions.
Preparing non-medical summaries of medical procedures as assigned.
Completing optional independent projects and exercises relating to medical conditions and diseases.
Completing assigned multimedia exercises and projects relating to medical conditions and diseases.
Developing presentations and using the library for assigned searches of periodic literature.
Evaluate and analyze short vignettes describing and illustrating disease conditions, signs, symptoms, etiology, diagnostic tests, and treatment.
Review medical records to abstract diagnosis, treatment, laboratory and x-ray information.
Distinguish among various body systems, structures, and functions as they are impacted by the processes of diseases and conditions.
